speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what is the likelihood of severe transboundary haze affecting Singapore this year; (b) what are the measures needed to prepare for such a possibility; and (c) how can the public be better prepared to mitigate the impact of severe transboundary haze.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And if Member Mr Yip is satisfied with the answer given, he may wish to withdraw the Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The ASMC has also forecasted that a positive Indian Ocean Dipole is likely to develop between July and August 2023.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) has worked with retail pharmacies to ensure sufficient stock of N95 masks.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MOH maintains a stockpile of N95 masks and is prepared to release masks to retail pharmacies, should the need arises.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There are also plans by the Inter-Agency Haze Task Force to work with the People's Association (PA) to distribute masks to low-income and vulnerable residents in the event of a severe haze episode.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: All classrooms of primary and secondary schools, MOE Kindergartens and special education schools are equipped with air purifiers to enhance the well-being of students during a haze episode.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Preschools are similarly required to ensure sufficient air purifiers to accommodate children in the event of haze.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MOH has advised medical practitioners on how to manage and treat patients with haze-related conditions, such as asthma or Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MOH has also advised all Public Healthcare Institutions (PHIs) on capacity mitigating measures in view of a potential increase in hospital admissions due to haze-related illnesses.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MOH has also worked with PHIs, including nursing homes, to ensure that they have adequate air-purifying equipment and medical supplies.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members of the public have been advised to refer to MOH's health advisories and to make preparations, such as ensuring that they have air purifiers in good working condition and N95 masks for prolonged outdoor activities during haze.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To stay up to date on the latest air quality situation, members of the public can visit NEA website, MyENV app and the haze microsite at haze.gov.sg.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will the Ministry consider working with the PA to establish haze sanctuaries, like using the Residents' Committees (RCs) or other community features, especially for our seniors who may not have the adequate N95 masks, air purifiers or air-conditioners in their homes?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: First of all, if you are unwell and you are elderly, you may wish to stay home and reduce your outdoor activities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: You may also draw the curtains of your house and have natural ventilation available.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: A mask is always helpful, especially if you are going outdoors for a prolonged period of time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Having said that, I would like to take up the Member's suggestions about working with PA to create spaces for the vulnerable segment of the population to seek rest for some period of time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we would very much like to thank the Member for that suggestion.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I understand the Minister had just attended the conference on ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control, the establishment of that.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Indeed, the Member is correct to say that we have recently met.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is the Ministerial Standing Committee comprising Ministers from the southern region of ASEAN.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The ASMC, which is hosted in Singapore, gave a comprehensive prediction, forecasts of the weather, that has been well accepted and also supported by the respective meteorological services centres in the respective countries.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, I think that is the general agreement about the likelihood, the risk level of a drier El Niño setting in the next few months.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And we have a good understanding about the assistance that Singapore has offered to the countries as well, should the need arise.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We had a good discussion also on the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control (ACC THPC).

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our discussion with the Indonesian government has always been very positive.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Over the last few years, significant effort has been put in on the Indonesian government's part on monitoring, as well as on supervisory, regulatory, as well as building up capability for firefighting.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Of course, we are helped by good weather in the last few years.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But this year, again, I think that there is common affirmation of the need to monitor the dry season carefully and also to act quickly to fight fires.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Because some of our elders and some of our residents might not have access to cooling devices or just cool environments.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will definitely take up that suggestion as well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These are all important nodes of community support on the ground; it is actually the result of many, many decades of hard work of building up assets, such as RCs, CCs, I would not say well-equipped, but which are prepared to handle some of these local exigencies when the need arises.
